label: 287(g) MOAs Active
contestNote: ACLU contends 287(g) leads to racial profiling and use on non-violent immigrants; Virginia passed HB1441/SB783 (effective July 1, 2026) restricting 287(g) participation. ICE offering $100K+ in vehicles and equipment as financial incentive to sign — covering 39 states and 2 territories. FWD.us estimates total incentives could reach $2B in 2026. New Hampshire police received over $300,000 in ICE stipend payments after one year. New Mexico, Maine, and Maryland enacted bans on 287(g) participation. 1,843 agencies as of May 19.

label: Deaths in Custody (FY2026, partial)
source: ICE.gov / Al Jazeera / PHR (as of May 1, 2026)
deltaNote: Calendar year 2026 total: 18 (through Apr 28); FY2026 (Oct 2025–May 2026): 30+ deaths — far exceeding FY2004 record of 28. 48+ since Trump took office Jan 2025. April 28: Denny Adan Gonzalez (33, Cuban) died at Stewart Detention Center — 5th apparent suicide of 2026, was in solitary confinement. ICE stopped paying for third-party medical care Oct 3, 2025. PHR: 95% of deaths likely preventable with adequate medical care. Pace: roughly one death every 6 days.

label: FY2025 Total Removals (Trump Year 1)
contestNote: ICE combines ~330,000 formal removals and ~110,000 voluntary returns — a methodology that inflates comparisons to prior administrations. Formal removals alone do not exceed FY2013 record of 432,201. ICE has now set an official target of 1 million removals per year. Total since inauguration (Jan 2025 through ~May 7, 2026): ~570,000, per Border Czar Tom Homan (NPR, May 7, 2026). FY2026 pace: ~1,286 removals/day as of April 4 — annualized ~470,000.
deltaNote: vs. ~271,000 in FY2024; total since inauguration: ~570,000 (Homan, May 7, 2026)

deltaNote: Down from 8,347/week (5-wk avg) before Feb 4, 2026 after Minneapolis agent pullback. Dec 2025 peak was ~40,000/month. Non-criminal share fell from 46% to 41%. Arrests surged in KY, IN, NC, and FL despite national decline.

label: Detainees Held Over 1 Year
deltaNote: Up from 998 in October 2025, more than doubling in 6 months as ICE detention expansion accelerates. The El Gamal family — Egyptian mother and 5 children — spent 320+ days in detention before their release April 26, 2026 following an aborted deportation flight.

label: ICE/CBP Reconciliation Package (2026)
source: CBO / Senate Budget Committee / Senate Parliamentarian (May 20, 2026)
contestNote: Senate Judiciary Committee: $39.2B; Senate Homeland Security: $32.5B; combined total: $71.7B. House passed 215-211 on April 30 with zero Democratic support. Senate Budget Committee voted 11-10 on May 20 to report the combined package to the full Senate floor — clearing the last procedural hurdle before a final vote. Senate Parliamentarian struck multiple provisions May 14-15 as Byrd Rule violations; Republicans rewrote struck sections before May 20 Budget Committee vote. Trump's June 1 signing deadline looms. Package funds 100,000+ detention beds, deportation flight expansion, CBP staffing, and border infrastructure. No independent oversight provisions, no use-of-force standards, no minimum medical care requirements despite 30+ FY2026 custody deaths.
deltaNote: Senate Budget Committee advanced to floor May 20 (11-10 vote). Largest single-year immigration enforcement investment in U.S. history if enacted — roughly 8× ICE's FY2024 base budget of $9.1B. Final Senate floor vote expected week of May 20.
